results.title: NIGERIA SIGNS $30M DEVELOPMENT GRANT AGREEMENT WITH CHINA.
results.description:
NIGERIA SIGNS $30M DEVELOPMENT GRANT AGREEMENT WITH CHINA.

Nigeria and China have signed a 200-million-yuan agreement, worth approximately US$30 million, to finance small-scale development projects across Nigeria.

Chinese Ambassador Yu Dunhai described the proposed interventions as “small but beautiful” projects designed to deliver practical results and improve people's livelihoods.

Minister of Budget and Economic Planning Abubakar Bagudu said:

• State governments have submitted project proposals.
• The proposals will be reviewed and consolidated.
• Nigeria and China will jointly identify projects for funding.
• The initiative is intended to address local development needs.
Importantly, the $30 million is a grant, not a commercial loan.
However, the specific projects, beneficiary communities and implementation timetable have not yet been announced.
The real measure of success will be whether the money translates into completed projects that Nigerians can see and benefit from.

Which communities and projects should receive priority?

results.title: From Stability to Opportunity: Reflections on Nigeria’s Engagement with Asia In Beijing, Central Bank of Nigeria @cenbank Governor Olayemi C
results.description:
From Stability to Opportunity: Reflections on Nigeria’s Engagement with Asia

In Beijing, Central Bank of Nigeria @cenbank Governor Olayemi Cardoso (@olayemicardoso1) led discussions across two major forums aimed at expanding Nigeria’s economic and financial ties with China.

The first gathering brought together business executives, financial experts and industry stakeholders operating along the Nigeria–China trade corridor. Conversations centred on payment systems, foreign exchange, trade financing and the challenges businesses face when conducting cross-border transactions.

The second forum, organised in collaboration with ICBC, focused on investment opportunities within Nigeria’s financial markets. Institutional investors, development finance organisations and other market participants examined ways to encourage investment and create a more supportive environment for capital inflows.

Cardoso also highlighted the importance of improving remittance services for Nigerians living abroad. The CBN’s focus includes making international transfers more affordable, accessible and efficient, while strengthening the financial links between the diaspora and Nigeria’s domestic economy.

results.description:
2027: APC Youth Wing, Mummymen, Hails Tinubu’s Diplomatic Achievements

Mummymen, a youth wing of the All Progressives Congress (APC), has praised President Bola Tinubu’s diplomatic engagements, describing them as a means of creating economic opportunities for Nigerians. 

In a circulating graphic, the group urged Nigerians to support the continuity of the Renewed Hope Agenda

Among the achievements cited are the commercial phase of the US$1.1 billion Green Imperative Project with Brazil, signed in March 2025, and China’s zero-tariff access for eligible Nigerian exports, which took effect in May 2026.

 The group also referenced reported Nigeria-China trade figures of US$18 billion in the first half of 2026 and an 80 per cent year-on-year increase in Chinese imports from Nigeria. It argued that such partnerships could benefit farmers, exporters and local businesses, while calling for sustained efforts to expand domestic production and ensure Nigerians benefit from international economic agreements.
